posts.text:
Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's main airport, killing 13.

Plus: an "energy ceasefire" Ukraine says it never heard of, India's voter-roll protests, Pakistan takes over a province, and a deadly Red Sea crossing.

Five map stories, a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Houthi missiles struck King Khalid airport in Riyadh on Saturday, killing 13 (BBC, Guardian, NYT). A second strike hit a terminal Sunday and Saudi Arabia extended its flight suspension.

The Yemen war now reaches the Saudi capital.

2/ Trump announced Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop hitting energy infrastructure (DW). Zelenskyy: "news to me"; the Kremlin rejected a 60-day truce offer (Guardian). Kyiv says Russia is already violating it (Al Jazeera).

3/ India's opposition marched to the Supreme Court demanding the election chief resign after thousands were detained in Delhi (BBC, Al Jazeera, NYT). The Guardian says 130m names were removed from the electoral roll.

4/ Pakistan's president declared an emergency and suspended the PTI-led government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; hundreds of PTI politicians were detained (Guardian). Islamabad cites militant violence (NYT).

5/ 139 people died when a boat carrying 305 capsized near Obock, Djibouti, en route to Yemen (BBC, UN). The NYT says it is among the deadliest wrecks on the route; 15 children's bodies were recovered.

Closing map: oil production, 2024. Russia, the US and Saudi Arabia share the top band, which is why strikes on Riyadh's airport and on Russian and Ukrainian energy sites ripple worldwide.
